tokens: he is bound by his oath

en.23:1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:
en.23:2: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
en.23:3: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.
en.23:4: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
en.23:5: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.
en.23:6: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,
en.23:7: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.
en.23:8: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
en.23:9: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
en.23:10: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.
en.23:11: The greatest among you shall be your servant.
en.23:12: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
en.23:13: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.
en.23:15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.
en.23:16: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’
en.23:17: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?
en.23:18: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’
en.23:19: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?
en.23:20: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
en.23:21: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.
en.23:22: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.
en.23:23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.
en.23:24: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
en.23:25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
en.23:26: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.
en.23:27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.
en.23:28: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.
en.23:29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.
en.23:30: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
en.23:31: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
en.23:32: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.
en.23:33: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?
en.23:34: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.
en.23:35: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
en.23:36: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

en.12:38: In His teaching Jesus also said, “Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces,
en.12:39: and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
en.12:40: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”

en.11:37: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
en.11:38: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
en.11:39: Then the Lord said, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
en.11:40: You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?
en.11:41: But give as alms the things that are within you, and behold, everything will be clean for you.
en.11:42: Woe to you Pharisees! For you pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
en.11:43: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
en.11:44: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.”
en.11:45: One of the experts in the law told Him, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.”
en.11:46: “Woe to you as well, experts in the law!” He replied. “For you weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.
en.11:47: Woe to you! For you build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.
en.11:48: So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
en.11:49: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’
en.11:50: As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world,
en.11:51: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
en.11:52: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”
en.11:53: As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things,
en.11:54: waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
en.20:45: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,
en.20:46: “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
en.20:47: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
